turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll take the obs before Dr Nguyen calls you in. Blood pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four, pulse seventy-six. Reception's medication sheet has doxylamine twenty-five milligrams at night.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The doxylamine's wrong. He's on fifty, two tablets. I pack the weekly box, so I'm sure.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): I'll flag it and leave it for the doctor rather than guess. The cricket's on in the waiting room if you want it, but you should be called any minute.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm Dr Nguyen. Do come in, both of you. What brings you along today?
[SEG0005] person_4 (PATIENT): Good afternoon, Doctor. Thank you for fitting us in. I am quite fine, really. My wife considered a visit the proper course.
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's not fine. Since he was made redundant he's barely sleeping, and he doesn't want to do anything. I practically had to book it myself.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you came. May I call you David?
[SEG0008] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, David is perfectly all right.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Setting fine to one side, how have you been, in your own words?

[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): I have been rather tired. And my sleep has been poor. It began about two months ago. No, forgive me, that is incorrect. It has been four months, since the redundancy in early February.
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Early Feb, yes. Project manager, logistics firm in Parramatta. They shut his division. He came home with a cardboard box and sat in the car for twenty minutes.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry, that is a lot to carry. What does a bad night actually look like?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): I go to bed near eleven. I lie awake until two, sometimes three, and I wake again before six. Four hours would be a generous estimate.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is the daytime energy only from the short sleep, or low even after a slightly better night?
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): Low regardless. Simple tasks require a surprising effort. Preparing a meal feels oddly heavy.

[SEG0016] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The interest has gone too. He coached the under-twelves Saturdays, not once since March. I put the footy on and he stares through it. Washed a clean cup during his favourite show the other night, which is not him.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): David, does that fit? Less a matter of tiredness alone, and more that you're not looking forward to things?
[SEG0018] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes. I regret that it does. I do not look forward to a great deal. I had hoped it was merely fatigue.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the mood itself?
[SEG0020] person_4 (PATIENT): Flat. Not tearful, particularly. I stay polite. There is very little feeling underneath.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Appetite or weight, any change?
[SEG0022] person_4 (PATIENT): Appetite is somewhat reduced. I do not think the weight has dropped a great deal.
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Trousers are looser. A couple of kilos, I'd say, nothing drastic. He eats if I plate it up, just less.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): I ask this of everyone when mood has been low for a stretch, and there is no wrong answer. Have you had thoughts of harming yourself, or of not wanting to go on?
[SEG0025] person_4 (PATIENT): No. I have not had those thoughts. I want that to be clear. I do not wish to harm myself, and I do not wish to die.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, I'll record that plainly. Alcohol, while all this has been going on?
[SEG0027] person_4 (PATIENT): Unchanged. One glass of red with dinner, three or four evenings a week, as for many years. Nothing more.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): The chart says doxylamine twenty-five milligrams at night. Are you taking that?
[SEG0029] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes. Restavit, from the chemist. One tablet, twenty-five milligrams, most nights. It helps only modestly.
[SEG0030] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's two tablets. Fifty milligrams. For about the last month, because one did nothing. He doesn't remember it clearly in the morning.
[SEG0031] person_4 (PATIENT): With respect, that is not so. I take a single tablet. I would not double it without advice.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the sheet says twenty-five, you say twenty-five, and your wife says fifty. I won't force an agreement today. Bring the box and the weekly pack and we'll pin it down. Anything else tried, melatonin, or an antidepressant?
[SEG0033] person_4 (PATIENT): Never an antidepressant. I bought melatonin, three milligrams, and stopped after a week. It did nothing at all.

[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me reflect this back. Four months since the redundancy: broken sleep, low energy, loss of interest, flat mood, appetite a little down, perhaps a small change in the trousers, no thoughts of self-harm, usual wine, doxylamine most nights but the dose not agreed. Have I got you?
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes. That is accurate. I apologise for saying I was fine at the outset. I am not fine. It has been difficult to state that formally.
[SEG0036] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's more than he's told his brother. I'll take it.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): My impression, and I stress it is provisional, is a depressive episode brought on in the setting of the job loss. Low mood, lost interest, poor energy and poor sleep for these months. I do not think we should start medication for it today.
[SEG0038] person_4 (PATIENT): I would prefer not to commence anything today. I should like time to consider it properly.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Agreed, no script today. If the sleep and the flat mood have not eased in four weeks, we can discuss starting sertraline, usually fifty milligrams each morning. Meanwhile, stick to the smallest doxylamine dose that helps, and skip nights when you can. Same wake time every day, phone out of the bedroom, and a short wind-down before bed.

[SEG0040] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll bring the Restavit box. And I'll get him back walking the dog in the mornings. He used to take her every day before work. Kelpie, loses the plot if the walk's missed, but anyway.

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Even ten minutes is worth it. I'll see you in four weeks regardless, and the desk can book it on the way out. If you ever felt unsafe before that, go to emergency or call Lifeline, thirteen eleven fourteen. You've said those thoughts aren't there, and I want the door left open anyway.
[SEG0042] person_4 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. We will return in four weeks, and I shall be direct with you.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
